lab.title: Lab
lab.subtitle: Three studies in scroll. Here the scrollbar is not navigation — it is the playhead.
lab.reducedMotion: Your system asks for reduced motion, so this renders its final state directly.

scrollVideo.name: Scroll as playhead
scrollVideo.summary: Not one video tag on the page. Every frame is an image; scroll far enough and it draws that frame.
scrollVideo.note: A 90-frame sequence with scroll progress mapped to a frame number. Scrolling back just draws backwards — there is no reverse-playback stutter.
scrollVideo.captionOneBody: Scroll progress becomes a frame number; the canvas only paints that frame.
scrollVideo.captionTwoBody: With no playback timeline, scrolling up simply draws in reverse.

dissolve.name: Dissolve
dissolve.summary: An image eaten away by a scalar field and a threshold, so the front breaks into organic clumps instead of a straight edge.
dissolve.note: A vertical gradient leads, low-frequency fbm crumbles the edge, high-frequency speckle adds grain. The threshold sweeps the screen as you scroll.
dissolve.headline: An edge is not a line
dissolve.body: The dissolve front is driven by a noise field, so it reads like paper wicking water rather than a curtain being drawn.
dissolve.tail: Scroll back and it grows in again.
dissolve.fallback: No WebGL available here, so this falls back to the static composition.

meltingText.name: Melting type
meltingText.summary: Letters congeal into one sticky liquid, then melt down into clean glyphs.
meltingText.note: A gaussian blur bleeds each glyph outward and an alpha threshold pushes anything past 30% opacity back to solid — where two blurred neighbours overlap, they fuse.
